mt: 'WALTER P. REUTHER LIBRARY' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE LIBRARY AT ITS GRAIN; AN APPOINTMENT ADVISED WHERE THE LIBRARY SAYS NONE IS REQUIRED; THE UAW'S GIFT OF THE BUILDING NOT CARRIED
d: THE LIBRARY, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Walter P. Reuther Library, Archives of Labor and Urban Affairs is the largest labor archive in North America, located on the campus of Wayne State University at 5401 Cass Ave in Detroit, Michigan.' History (1960, 1975, 1991); labor, urban and university collections; visiting and research. Seven cards: the library, Wayne State (three), Wikipedia, Project MUSE, DETROITography.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the library, the Overview gives its history, its collections and how to use them, and offers to guide a visit.
findings: THE ACCESS RULE RESTATED. 'Researchers should schedule a research appointment in advance with Reference Archivist Kristen Chinery.' The library's About page, saved the same day: 'The collections housed in the Reuther Library are freely open to the public. Appointments are not required'.

THE CUSTODIAN OF THE UNIONS' OWN RECORDS. 'Serves as the official repository for major labor unions and organizations, including the United Automobile Workers (UAW)'. The building was 'constructed with funds given to Wayne State University by the United Automobile, Aerospace, and Agricultural Implement Workers of America' (the library's page); the composition gives the years of the building and wing without the gift. #1725 asks of such an archive whether it keeps the records of the oppositions inside the unions it holds; neither the composition nor the saved pages say.
analysis: An accurate account of the library's history and holdings, with one access rule stated against the library's own page and its funding by the union whose records it keeps not carried.
per_note: The library and university named; the library's site among the cards.
